### 2026-10-06 – October 6:

**2.5h**

October 6:
I originally set out to just start the project for today, but I had a few goals in mind after wrapping my head around what I really needed to do.

 - figure out what I wanted to build and post a video on it: originally, I tried to use TinkerCad, but that proved a little too time-consuming, so I built a 2d version in Miro instead.

![scrapped 3d model](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/0a2a646749e0c0804339df1dda0d997865e3ea3e225083fc0a8930e67ab87f85.png)

 - get my repo check done, I used claude code for the majority of this (more on this later!), specifically the PCD on KiCad and the firmware. But after revising the docs, I realized that it wasn't faithful to the terms and values of half-life. And next session, I'll go back, delete everything, and only use the previously generated work as a guide while doing it ALL MYSELF!

 - Things for set up I did do, setting up hackatime was challenging for me, for some reason, I was only seeing other... on the list dropdown, but after using Claude PROPERLY, finagling with GitHub repos and local repos, it all worked out and I could finally track my code hours

![I couldn't see anything past the pesky other..., but now maybe I see too much?](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/ac10ddbdba8ae42f029c4aef1000bec364df1b1ebc03c14147069ec26aa2dc03.png)

 -  next session, I'll redo everything with proper guidance and work, and I'll finish the goals I originally set out to do ( finishing the GitHub checklist)

tldr: Learned all about the half-life process and how the program works. Learned the hard way to always check doc rules appropriately and use Claude Code appropriately, as a tool. Learned to work efficiently and focus on one task at a time.

### 2026-10-08 – October 8:

**3h**

October 8:
In the previous session, I wanted to start on the things that Claude Code had done for me before, but it became immediately clear that I had to finish the component list first. So, today I planned to finish the BOM file, getting all my components and parts down for my device. I didn't realize it would be so hard, though. I truly thought it would be a 1-hour task max.

1. I had a first iteration of the parts list. I thought it would be the last one, so I didn't take a screenshot. It was mostly full of negative things, but it was a great learning experience:
 - I didn't realize how interconnected devices were; it didn't have wiring, insulation, and the battery pack was quite simplistic
 - It really didn't follow my original plan. I had an external battery, an overkill motor, and components of wildly different sizes.
 - At this point, my budget was looking great, sitting at ~$40.

![1st+2nd list iteration](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/8a41e68aaddc04d6a3f72590db450ffaa3b8d762226357c086dc86cc75f39e80.png)

2. My next iteration was extremely different. I realized how many issues my original list/plan had, and I had to change many components entirely. During the process, I also learned more about how my device would work, and it changed my original design and view of what it should look like. Of course, I still ran into many issues.
 - My budget was growing higher and higher, and I thought that instead of compromising quality, I would just move my project to funding tier 3.
![2nd list iteration](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/dd375f65641b6b8f40520db66f2c4d06d94fa79a9338902c193a39bd0be95b6a.png)
 - It really opened up my eyes to the process of creating a new product; everything was relatively expensive, but the shipping was the real killer. I had to rely on Amazon HEAVILY in order to get past shipping costs.
 - After finagling with different products and shipping settings, I managed to maximize my quality vs budget ratio, and finally arrived at a list that I was happy with. I ran it through Claude, and it said that my list was good.
![Final part list](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6we3n02G0pmeDEZa8smpIoxMjgf1WM2Q/9f03670be4332630dfb4bc120f841b11ff51e6775dcf3058b0fcae8529f39bf5.png)

Hopefully, I can have my next session tomorrow. I'd like to start on the PCB and design.

tldr: Finding components is hard, and it takes a lot longer than I thought. I'm impressed by how cheap some factories can make items. I understand electronics pricing now. Starting over isn't a bad thing, and don't compromise on quality. Tomorrow is the start of design.
